errors: Own simulator first let only one car board at a time, which made the lobby the bottleneck when the interval was shorter than a full car's boarding time (6 x 1600 kg on 6 floors showed wait/interval up to 9). Fixed before any number was published: the next car opens to the queue once the current one has a full load boarding.
Post front matter failed writing.test.mjs twice (description 169 > 160 chars, seo_title 79 > 70); caught by venture-preflight before push.

First CI run red on two checks venture-preflight does not run: check_step_grid.py (capacityFactor min=1 step=5) and check_doc_counts.py (PRODUCT_PLAYBOOK.md venture count 1338 vs tree 1366, drift that predates this PR). Both fixed in a follow-up commit.

doc_friction.issue: My first idea (duct sizing) already existed inside hvac-load-calc as ducts.html; duplicate_check.py screens VENTURE.yaml descriptions, so a feature inside another venture is only found by reading its README. Cost one detour.

The siblings orphan budget and the visible-FAQ rule only surface in venture-preflight's site tests; the definition-of-done list does not mention that a new tool needs an inbound link from a sibling tool.

Preflight reported clean, yet CI's changed-ventures and validate jobs failed on check_doc_counts.py and check_step_grid.py; neither is in the preflight, so a 'clean' preflight still meant a red first CI run.

notes: Explore idea: elevator (lift) traffic analysis, a new venture. Up-peak RTT per Barney & dos Santos with Peters (2000) corrections (jerk-limited flight times, unequal floors, express zone), verified: flight-time closed forms vs numerical integration to 1e-6 s; S and H vs Monte Carlo; formula RTT vs 20,000 sampled trips within -0.83%..+1.39% over 27 buildings. Design search over lifts/loads/speeds. Poisson-arrival lobby simulation: median mean wait / interval 0.50-0.51 at 80% of the formula's handling capacity and 0.92-1.03 at 100%, across dwell 4-15 s (bench/grid.md, regenerated byte-for-byte by the tests). Driven in headless Chromium at 1280/390 px, no console errors or overflow. Next: lunch-time two-way traffic and general analysis with multiple entrances. No agent doc in docs/reports: README and how-it-works carry what the next run needs.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: an engineer implementing and verifying the RTT method, a simulator and a page from the published papers

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
